concepts.definition: Capacity, right, or power to exercise control or authority in a relation, independent of any one source-language lexeme.
concepts.scope_note: Source-language words map here only through contextual lexical-sense analysis. No Arabic, Hebrew, Greek, or other lexeme is automatically equivalent to this concept.
notes: The As-Saffat 37:30 worked example maps a contextual sense of سُلْطَانٍ to this concept as a research assertion; the lexeme itself is not the ontology identity.

concepts.definition: Exceeding, violating, or crossing a proper limit, constraint, or norm in the evaluated context.
concepts.scope_note: The exact type of limit or norm is contextual and must not be inferred solely from an English or Indonesian label.
notes: Cross-language terms must map through lexical/contextual sense analysis, not translation-string matching.

concepts.definition: A derived positive target in which conduct or state is realigned with a valid boundary identified by a reviewed Witness derivation.
concepts.scope_note: This concept is a downstream target and must not be back-projected into source text as direct lexical meaning.
notes: This is not claimed as a direct lexical concept in As-Saffat 37:30.
